milestones.label: Newton's De analysi written
milestones.work: I. Newton, De analysi per aequationes numero terminorum infinitas (written 1669; published 1711)
milestones.description: Newton's manuscript uses infinite series for quadratures but circulated only privately until later publication.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia dates the manuscript to 1669 and its publication to 1711

milestones.note: Private manuscript, so a precursor and not the public start. Priority dispute with Leibniz is not adjudicated here.

milestones.label: Leibniz publishes the differential calculus
milestones.work: G. W. Leibniz, Nova methodus pro maximis et minimis, Acta Eruditorum (October 1684)
milestones.description: The first published exposition of the calculus, with the differential notation.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia: published in Acta Eruditorum, October 1684, described as the first published work on calculus

works.citation: Nova methodus pro maximis et minimis
De analysi per aequationes numero terminorum infinitas

notes: Only Wikipedia pages read; no bibliographic-record check, so confidence is medium (grade C). Not searched: first textbook (L'Hopital 1696), naming/institution milestones.

canonicalName: Graph theory from the Konigsberg bridges

milestones.label: Euler's Konigsberg paper published
milestones.work: L. Euler, Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis, Commentarii Academiae Scientiarum Petropolitanae 8 (1736; published 1741)
milestones.description: Euler shows the bridge walk is impossible by reducing the problem to the parity of the degrees of a network.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia: presented 26 August 1735, published in the Commentarii in 1741; Euler Archive record E53

milestones.note: Presented 1735, formalised 1736; publication year governs. Hierholzer later proved sufficiency of the condition (year not given on the page).

works.citation: Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis

notes: Euler Archive page E53 loaded and mentions 1741; contents otherwise unread. Not verified: Kirchhoff 1847 (inherited citation), Konig's 1936 book, coinage of 'graph'; add after checking sources.

canonicalName: Fourier series: heat flow to analysis

milestones.label: Fourier's heat memoir
milestones.work: J. Fourier, On the Propagation of Heat in Solid Bodies, memoir presented to the Paris Institute, 21 December 1807
milestones.description: The memoir expands arbitrary functions in sine series to solve the heat equation but was not published.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia: presented to the Paris Institute on 21 December 1807

milestones.note: Presented, not published; hence a precursor.

milestones.label: Theorie analytique de la chaleur
milestones.work: J. Fourier, Theorie analytique de la chaleur (Paris, 1822)
milestones.description: The treatise states that an arbitrary function can be expanded in trigonometric series and derives the heat equation.

notes: Dirichlet's 1829 convergence paper is an inherited citation but its date was not confirmed on the page read; left out of milestones until checked against a bibliographic record.

canonicalName: Klein's Erlangen programme: geometry as invariants of a group

milestones.label: Klein's Erlangen programme
milestones.work: F. Klein, Vergleichende Betrachtungen ueber neuere geometrische Forschungen (Erlangen, 1872)
milestones.description: Geometries are classified by the transformation groups whose invariants they study.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia: published 1872; later reprinted in Mathematische Annalen 43 (1893)

works.citation: Vergleichende Betrachtungen ueber neuere geometrische Forschungen

notes: Wikipedia only. Cartan's generalisation is mentioned on the page without a year, so not entered as a milestone.
